newsitem.title: USA: Tucson Electric seeks to refinance debt.
newsitem.headline: Tucson Electric seeks to refinance debt.

text.p: Tucson Electric Power Co said Friday it filed with the Arizona Corporation Commission (ACC) for authority to refinance a major portion of outstanding debt and implement a direct purchase stock plan.
The company said the request would allow it to:
-- extend debt maturities and letters of credit;
-- reduce the volatility of its capital costs;
-- modify or replace existing restrictive debt covenants;

"TEP faces significant financing requirements between 1999 and 2003," said Ira Adler, TEP chief financial officer, noting $192 million of the company's long-term debt obligations and letters of credit supporting $774 million of TEP's variable-rate debt obligations are scheduled to mature.
The company's application consists of four key components:
1. Refinancing up to $450 million of tax-exempt variable rate debt now backed by letters of credit. These refinancings are expected to be on a fixed-rate, unsecured basis.

2. Replacing TEP's current credit agreements with one or more new credit facilities. The company has credit commitments totalling more than $880 million. TEP believes replacement credit facilities will likely be smaller in size, have extended maturities or termination dates and contain less restrictive covenants than the existing credit facilities.

3. Refinancing up to $184 million in first mortgage bonds scheduled to mature between 1999 and 2003. TEP is requesting flexibility in the type of securities to be issued which may include new debt and/or equity securities.
4. Implementing a direct stock purchase plan, making the company's common stock more accessible to small investors. TEP said it would issue up to one million shares of common stock under the plan.
"The company's credit agreements presently contain covenants restricting the restoration of common dividend payments," said Adler.
"Elimination of these covenants is essential if TEP is to attract additional equity capital on reasonable terms."
Tucson Electric Power Co is an investor-owned utility engaged in the generation, purchase, transmission, distribution and sale of electric energy to retail and wholesale customers.
